title: flag when a slice note recorded after the spec contradicts the spec's Implement or test text, before the implementer starts

sections.heading: Why
sections.body:
The spec check judges a slice's spec as it stands. It does not notice a slice note recorded after the spec was written that contradicts the spec. The reviewer found this in ork run ork-20261126-004139-f69b on S592. Note adj 596 (2026-11-26) said to list each non-Go file, but Implement step 3 and the test forbade naming paths. Nothing flagged the conflict before the implementer started.

Owner decision (adj 603, key `spec.note-after-spec-check`, answer "both"):
- Code flags every slice note recorded after the spec was last written. It uses the note's `created_at` from `slicer show` and the time of the newest `edit` or `promote` entry in `slicer log`.
- The spec check then judges each flagged note against Implement and Failing tests. It raises an owner question when one conflicts.

The owner's answer to that question is appended to Implement through `RecordSpecAnswers`. That counts as a write of the spec, so the note stops being flagged afterwards.

Owner decisions, 2026-11-26: adj 603 (code flags notes recorded after the spec; the spec check judges each against Implement and tests) and adj 608 (the spec fingerprint hashes flagged note ids, so a new note re-runs the check once).

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
- TestLastSpecWriteReadsTheNewestEditOrPromote (`internal/slicercli/slicercli_test.go`): with a fake `slicer log --item S10 --action edit --action promote --limit 1 --json --lean --root /projects/ork` that prints one entry with `"when":"2026-11-26T01:00:00Z"`, `LastSpecWrite` returns that time and `true`. With a reply of `[]` it returns `false` and no error. A slicer error keeps its code, as `RelayStats` does.
- TestNotesAfterSpecWriteKeepsOnlyLaterNotes (`internal/engine/specnotes_test.go`): `NotesAfterSpecWrite` takes `slicer show` JSON with notes at 01:00:00Z, 02:00:00Z and 03:00:00Z, and a last write of 02:00:00Z.
  - It returns only the 03:00:00Z note: id, `created_at`, `by`, `kind` and text.
  - A note at exactly the write time is not flagged.
  - A retracted note (`retracted_at` set) is not flagged, even if it is later.
  - A note with an unparseable `created_at` returns an error that names the note id.
- TestSpecNotesAfterWriteSkipsTheLogWithoutNotes (`internal/engine/specnotes_test.go`): `SpecNotesAfterWrite` makes no `slicer log` call when the item has no note records.
  - With notes but no `edit` or `promote` entry in the log, it flags nothing.
  - With notes and a newer write entry, it flags only the later notes.
- TestSpecCheckBriefListsNotesRecordedAfterTheSpec (`internal/engine/speccheck_test.go`): `RunSpecCheck` over S10 and S11, where S10 has a note newer than its last write and S11 has none.
  - The role's brief holds a "Notes recorded after the spec" section that names S10, the note id, its `created_at` and its text.
  - That section does not name S11.
- TestSpecCheckBriefHasNoNotesSectionWhenNoneAreFlagged (`internal/engine/speccheck_test.go`): when no note is newer than the last write, the brief has no "Notes recorded after the spec" section.
- TestSpecCheckPromptJudgesNotesRecordedAfterTheSpec (`internal/roles/roles_test.go`): the spec-check prompt names the "Notes recorded after the spec" section. It tells the role to read each listed note against Implement and Failing tests. It asks one question for a conflicting note with the options `follow the note` and `follow the spec`, and no Decision key line. It asks nothing for a note that does not conflict. The prompt stays ASCII.
- TestSpecCheckRerunsACachedVerdictWhenANoteIsRecordedAfterTheSpec (`internal/daemon/speccheck_test.go`): this uses `newSpecRig`. A first check of S1 with no later notes runs the role once and ends Ready. A note newer than the spec's last write is then added to S1, and a second check runs the role again, which is 2 role requests in all. The second brief names the note.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
1. In `internal/slicercli/types.go` add `LogEntry` with `When`, `Item`, `Action`, `Note` and `By` fields and the slicer JSON tags `when`, `item`, `action`, `note` and `by`.
2. In `internal/slicercli/slicercli.go` add `func (c Client) LastSpecWrite(ctx context.Context, root, id string) (time.Time, bool, error)`.
   - It runs `slicer log --item ID --action edit --action promote --limit 1 --json --lean --root ROOT` through `clirun.RunJSON` and `checkID`.
   - It returns the newest entry's `when` parsed as RFC 3339, or `false` for an empty list.
   - slicer's `log` prints newest first (`slicer/src/slicer/cli_report.py:291`).
   - `edit` covers a section, the lead or the boundary (`slicer/src/slicer/ops.py:2107`, `:2300`, `:2312`); `promote` is the first write (`ops.py:729`).
3. Create `internal/engine/specnotes.go` with a `FlaggedNote` struct (id, created_at, by, kind, text) and two functions.
   - `NotesAfterSpecWrite(raw []byte, wrote time.Time) ([]FlaggedNote, error)` is pure. It reads `note_records` from the `slicer show --json --lean` output. It keeps a record whose `created_at` is strictly after `wrote` and whose `retracted_at` is empty. An unparseable `created_at` is an error that names the note id.
   - `SpecNotesAfterWrite(ctx, d Deps, root, id string, raw []byte) ([]FlaggedNote, error)` returns nothing and makes no `slicer log` call when `raw` holds no live note record. Otherwise it calls `d.Slicer.LastSpecWrite`, flags nothing when there is no write entry, and else returns `NotesAfterSpecWrite`.
4. In `runSpecCheckOnce` (`internal/engine/speccheck.go`, the loop over `cfg.Items` at line 379) call `SpecNotesAfterWrite` for each item and keep the result by id.
   - Append a `BriefSection` titled "Notes recorded after the spec" to the `Sections` of the spec-check brief (line 418).
   - For each item with flagged notes it lists the item id and one line per note with id, `created_at`, `by`, `kind` and full text.
   - It adds no section when no item has a flagged note.
5. In `internal/roles/prompts/spec-check.md` add a step to the **Spec check** list.
   - When the brief lists "Notes recorded after the spec", read each note against the slice's Implement and Failing tests, and its Files and Check.
   - A note that those sections contradict, or do not carry out, is a conflict. Ask one question for the slice, with exactly two options: `follow the note` (the implementer follows the note over the conflicting spec text) and `follow the spec` (the spec stands and the note is set aside). Omit the Decision key line.
   - Ask nothing for a note that does not conflict. The existing rule that a gap closable by reading code is not a question still applies.
6. Cached verdicts: make a flagged note recorded after a verdict was cached run the check again, by the mechanism the owner picks in `spec.note-after-spec-cache` (see Owner needed). The change is in `internal/daemon/speccheck.go` and in the fingerprint sites the chosen option touches. A slice with no flagged note keeps today's behaviour and cache keys.
7. In `docs/design.md`, under the **Spec check** bullet, add a short paragraph. It says that ork flags every slice note recorded after the spec was last written, that the check judges each flagged note against Implement and Failing tests, and that an owner's answer re-writes Implement and so clears the flag (adj 603, `spec.note-after-spec-check`).
8. Run `gofmt -l .` and `go vet ./...`. Run `slicer check --root /home/jon/code/squalor-xyz/ork`.
